keyVerseText: And out of the tribe of Asher, Mishal with her suburbs, Abdon with her suburbs,
rootMeaning: The name עַבְדוֹן (ʻAbdôwn) derives from the Hebrew root עָבַד (ʻâbad), which fundamentally means 'to serve' or 'to be in bondage.' This root conveys the idea of servitude or labor, encompassing both the literal sense of working or serving and the figurative sense of submission or devotion. The etymology highlights a core theme of service, suggesting that the name ʻAbdôwn carries the connotation of one who is a servant or bonded in service, which enriches the understanding beyond the mere transliteration of a proper name.
usageInScripture: The word עַבְדוֹן appears eight times in Scripture, primarily as a proper name. It refers to four individuals: a judge of Israel, a Benjamite, a Gibeonite, and a son of Micah, as well as a Levitical city in the tribe of Asher. The top translations consistently render it as 'Abdon' or variations thereof, indicating its primary use as a personal or place name rather than a common noun. This consistent translation underscores its identity as a name linked to servitude or service, reflecting the root meaning embedded in its use.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עַבְדוֹן as rooted in servitude deepens the theological appreciation of biblical leadership and community. The judge Abdon, for example, exemplifies one who serves God's people, embodying the ideal of leadership as service rather than dominion. This aligns with the New Testament revelation of Christ as the ultimate servant-leader who came to serve and give His life for many. The notion of being 'bond-servants' of God resonates through the biblical narrative, inviting believers to embrace humble service as a reflection of divine calling and identity. The name ʻAbdôwn thus reminds the faithful that true honor and purpose are found in devoted service to God and others.
keyVerseReflection: Joshua 21:30 mentions 'Abdon with her suburbs' as a Levitical city within the tribe of Asher, highlighting the city's role in the distribution of land for the Levites. The use of the name עַבְדוֹן here connects the place to the theme of service, as the Levites were set apart to serve in the tabernacle and later the temple. This reinforces the idea that the city of Abdon was not merely a geographical location but a center of sacred service, symbolizing God's provision for those dedicated to His work among His people.
